@copilot Refactor the query callback advice in this PR to make the supported method signatures explicit and remove the runtime argument-array guessing. Update this existing PR directly, not a separate follow-up PR.

In `instrumentation/influxdb-2.4/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/influxdb/v2_4/InfluxDbImplInstrumentation.java`, replace `@Advice.AllArguments` and `@Advice.AssignReturned.ToAllArguments` in the asynchronous and chunked query advice with named, typed `@Advice.Argument` parameters and explicit `@Advice.AssignReturned.ToArguments` mappings for the wrapped callbacks. Split the chunked advice by supported signature instead of inspecting `arguments[2]`, array lengths, or callback runtime types. Match each signature explicitly. Preserve the non-chunked asynchronous `query(Query, Consumer, Consumer)` path and all five chunked overloads: `query(Query, int, Consumer)`, `query(Query, int, BiConsumer)`, `query(Query, int, Consumer, Runnable)`, `query(Query, int, BiConsumer, Runnable)`, and `query(Query, int, BiConsumer, Runnable, Consumer)`.

Keep the existing `inline = false` approach and the typed wrapper helpers in `InfluxDbObjectWrapper.java`. Share query-span setup and cleanup where useful rather than copying that logic into every advice class, but keep the implementation simple. Do not merely move the array-length and `instanceof` dispatch into a helper. Preserve parent-context restoration for callbacks, nullable callback behavior, existing span lifetime and telemetry, synchronous query behavior, exception suppression, and balanced call-depth handling when overloads delegate to one another. Retain compatibility across the supported InfluxDB versions, including 2.4, without requiring newer library types in advice that must load on older versions.

Use the module's existing tests, including `InfluxDbClientTest.java` and the 2.4 compatibility suite, to verify the refactor. Add focused coverage only where needed to demonstrate callback context propagation for the supported callback signatures, completion/failure callbacks, and no duplicate query spans through overload delegation. Run the narrowest applicable formatting and validation commands, using `spotlessApply` directly rather than first running `spotlessCheck`. Keep this change limited to the callback-advice readability refactor and behavior-preserving supporting changes.

Keep callback wrapping conditional on instrumentation actually starting, and preserve the original parent context used by callbacks. Preserve existing span lifetime, telemetry, nullable callback behavior, exception suppression, typed argument mappings, supported InfluxDB versions including 2.4, and the existing `inline = false` approach.

Keep this a behavior-preserving AdviceScope refactor. threads.body: [Javaagent] If startup throws—for example, a context customizer's `onStart` hook throws—the enter advice suppresses the exception and returns null. The new exit advice then skips `end()`, leaving the call-depth increment in place. Subsequent InfluxDB queries and writes on that thread are treated as nested calls and lose their spans. Previously, exit advice decremented depth even when entry failed. Roll back the increment if initialization throws, then rethrow so the advice's suppression still handles the failure.

@copilot Fix the failed-start CallDepth regression in this existing PR. Update this PR directly, not a separate follow-up PR.

In `instrumentation/influxdb-2.4/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/influxdb/v2_4/InfluxDbQueryAdviceScope.java`, keep the current AdviceScope design, its non-null bookkeeping placeholders, and the exit-advice null checks. After `CallDepth` is incremented, guard fallible startup so a failure before returning the AdviceScope decrements exactly this invocation's increment and rethrows the original exception to the existing advice suppression. A narrow catch/decrement/rethrow guard is appropriate. Successful startup and successful no-span placeholder returns must leave the decrement to `end()`; do not use an unconditional finally decrement, reset the shared counter, or add an unconditional exit-side decrement that would double-balance failed startup.

This is an interim local fix for https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/issues/20667, which tracks a future shared failed-entry cleanup approach covering the entire enter advice and temporary thread state. Do not implement generic rollback machinery or expand into an audit of unrelated instrumentation in this PR. Preserve the single CallDepth lookup and clear lifecycle ownership.

Add focused regression coverage for an actual startup failure after the increment, followed by a healthy query and write on the same thread that still produce their InfluxDB spans. A one-shot throwing context customizer is one possible trigger; use the existing test infrastructure and the simplest supported trigger. Exercise suppressed enter-advice failure if feasible, rather than only an application exception or the already-covered null query. Preserve nested overload delegation, no duplicate spans, suppressed/no-span paths, callback parent context and nullability, span lifetime and telemetry, typed callback mappings, `inline = false`, and supported InfluxDB versions including 2.4. Do not refactor unrelated write advice.

Run the narrowest applicable `spotlessApply` task directly before relevant validation, and use the module's existing tests and InfluxDB 2.4 compatibility coverage. Keep changes limited to the startup rollback and focused regression coverage.
